policies.title: Current preferred 60-day waiver remains in force pending Gazette transition
policies.summary: Thailand's current Consular Affairs schedule continues to give these ordinary passports a 60-day exemption while the five replacement notices remain unpublished and non-operative.
conditions: This is the preferred current baseline for the listed valid ordinary national passports, for tourism and short-term business engagements for a stay not exceeding 60 days.

Thailand's 19 July government notice says all five replacement Ministry of Interior notices remain pending Royal Gazette publication and that current entry conditions remain in place until the new measures take effect.

The announced replacement is not current law. It must not be applied, end-dated or used for ranking until the Gazette texts are published, the stated 15-day commencement period elapses and their exact scopes are independently reviewed.
Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Myanmar and Timor-Leste retain separately modeled bilateral ordinary-passport routes and are not duplicated in this preferred-route policy.
The Thailand Digital Arrival Card remains a separate arrival declaration, not a visa or ETA. Work, residence, special documents, extensions and final admission remain outside this policy.

policies.title: Current 15-day arrival-visa cohort remains in force pending Gazette transition
policies.summary: The current Consular Affairs schedule continues to give these non-overlapping ordinary-passport nationalities a 15-day visa on arrival while the replacement notices remain unpublished.
conditions: The source's 31-entry arrival-visa schedule overlaps the 60-day waiver for 16 marked entries. This preferred-route policy contains only the remaining 15 ordinary-passport nationalities.
The current route permits a stay up to 15 days and remains in force until the replacement notices are published and their separate 15-day commencement period has elapsed.

The July proposal's Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia arrival-visa group is not operative. Belarus and Serbia remain in this current cohort, while Azerbaijan remains on the advance eVisa route until current law changes.
The Thailand Digital Arrival Card remains a separate arrival declaration, not a visa or ETA. Work, residence, special documents, extensions and final admission remain outside this policy.
